summary: Self-improving agent loop released March 2026 where a coding agent iterates on a training script, measures whether changes improve performance (5-min GPU budget), keeps improvements and rolls back regressions. Ran 700 experiments in 2 days, stacked 20 additive gains. 66k+ stars.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the tight measure-keep/discard loop is conceptually related to plan repair and retry. However, AgentForge already ships skill distillation (HID-188 tracks cross-run episodic memory). The self-evolving loop pattern is explicitly on the red-flag list in the evaluation criteria (prompt self-evolution). Backlog full (11 issues).

summary: LangGraph 1.0 (Oct 2025) + LangMem: agent memory library handling episodic, semantic (user preferences, summaries, behavioral patterns), and procedural memory across sessions. Built-in memory stores with MongoDB integration for cross-session persistence. LangMem has a unique prompt optimization feature.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — AgentForge already shipped skill distillation + planner injection (distillationAgent.ts, agentSkillRepository.ts). Cross-run episodic run-outcome memory is already tracked by open issue HID-188. No new gap identified beyond what is already tracked.

summary: Comparison of open-source agent memory frameworks 2026: Cognee (graph-native ECL pipeline), Mem0, Zep, Letta, MemGPT, Graphiti, LangMem. Dakera (May 2026) is a self-hosted Rust/RocksDB memory server with decay-weighted vector recall and hybrid BM25+HNSW retrieval, scoring 87.8% on LoCoMo benchmark.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — these are external memory server libraries for frameworks using API clients. AgentForge uses CLI subprocess agents with its own skill distillation layer. HID-188 already tracks cross-run episodic memory for AgentForge specifically.

summary: Major April 2026 update: native sandbox execution (file inspection, command running, code editing in controlled environments), model-native harness, background processing via Responses API, realtime TTS voice agents. TypeScript parity with Python. Provider-agnostic via Chat Completions API.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge deliberately uses CLI subprocess agents (not API clients) with its own deterministic state machine. The sandbox and multi-agent handoff patterns don't map to AgentForge's architecture. No gap opened by this release.

summary: Microsoft merged Semantic Kernel's enterprise features with AutoGen's multi-agent orchestration into Agent Framework 1.0 for .NET and Python. Targets enterprise compliance (EU AI Act) and large-scale multi-agent deployments.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — different language stack (.NET/Python vs Node.js TypeScript), enterprise compliance focus, API-client agent model. No direct architectural patterns applicable to AgentForge's CLI subprocess + state machine model.

source: Token cost telemetry and FinOps patterns for AI agents 2026
summary: OpenTelemetry-based AI observability patterns: tagging model invocations with feature_id, user_id, model_tier, tool_call_count, retrieval_size_kb. Prompt caching as 90% cost reduction. Per-task/per-user cost attribution dashboards. FinOps for AI rose from 31% to 98% practitioner adoption 2025→2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly relevant to HID-163 (per-run token cost and stage latency telemetry with budget enforcement), which already tracks this theme. The OpenTelemetry tagging patterns and prompt caching strategies could strengthen the HID-163 implementation. No new issue warranted.
